title: capparis domingensis subsp. grisebachii
intro: Capparis domingensis subsp. grisebachii, commonly known as the West Indian or Caribbean caper, is a plant species native to the Caribbean region. This plant is valued for its edible flowers and shoots, which are used as a vegetable or spice. Research has shown that Capparis domingensis subsp. grisebachii possesses various health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can aid in protecting against chronic diseases. The plant's bioactive constituents include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as reducing inflammation and oxidative stress.
